transcriptText:
First to act, at a full table... and first to act at six-handed. Should you open the same hands from both? Take a guess.

Opening is really about the players still to act behind you. Full table, the first seat has eight behind. Six-handed, only five. That's the same job as the fourth seat at a full table... not the first.

Count the danger. A premium hand, jacks or better or ace-king, is 3% of hands. With eight players behind you, someone holds one about 22% of the time. With five, about 14%. From the button, with two left, about 6%.

Your turn. Six-handed, from the cutoff... three players behind. Fewer hands to get through, so you open more. Fewer seats means fewer players to beat. Count who's behind you, then open wider.
